articleTitle: Simulation of the electric drive of a beam pumping unit and its comparative analysis for different operating frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In this paper, we intend to perform a simulation of the variable speed electric drive of a beam pumping unit, in which an asynchronous machine is powered through a frequency converter and is controlled by the Direct Torque Control technique. In the upward stroke of the pumping cycle, the asynchronous machine operates in motor regime and in the downward stroke it works in generator mode, which can be considered a braking regime The purpose of the simulation is to carry out an analysis of the variation of the main energy parameters when the electric drive operates at different frequencies. The results obtained for a specific pumping unit, however, have a high degree of validity also for other models of extraction equipment in Canadian version, which do not bring any essential changes in the modelling of the system.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optimal Character of Metaheuristic based Algorithms used in Closed Loop: Evaluation through simulation series
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: A stand-alone metaheuristic based algorithm can solve a specific optimal control problem, but the result is an offline “optimal” solution, which is a sequence of values assigned to the control inputs over the control horizon. Because this solution can be exploited only within an open-loop control structure, the algorithm has to be adapted in order to be used inside a closed-loop control structure as controller. But this adaptation and also the dynamics of the real process involve a degradation of the optimal character of the control structure, namely a decreasing of the performance index. This paper proposes a method for analyzing the behavior of the closed-loop based on three simulation models. Using this tool, one can state whether the solution implemented by the real-time control system has a proper quasi-optimal character.

articleTitle: Compact Isolated Speech Recognition on Raspberry-Pi based on Reaction Diffusion Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: A low complexity solution for speech recognition is proposed and its implementation on a resources constrained platform, namely the Raspberry-Pi is evaluated. In order to achieve good performance with limited resources, both the feature extractor and the classifier are specially designed. A special form of feature extractor, called RDT (reaction-diffusion transform) was optimized and evaluated in conjunction with a specially designed ELM (extreme learning machine) classifier. Optimization of parameters led to very good recognition rates (up to 100%) for a small dictionary of isolated sounds representing vocal commands for automotive applications. The real time factor is sub-unitary, ensuring the realization of real time identification using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design Study Case Overview for Naval Power Generation and Delivery
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper is an overview of the challenges presented of the power system design for a ship, especially for the Main Switchboard (MSB) design, pointing on the safety, fault tolerant of power system functional stages. In this paper we used the naval technical specification and came with solutions for a ship study case. In the end conclusions were drawn regarding the safety, precision, future performance and technical aspects of the study case.

articleTitle: The energetic performances of control at constant magnetic flux of an induction traction motor: Part 2 - Performances of control at constant rotor flux and comparative analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present and analyze the energetic performance of a traction induction motor for autonomous vehicles controlled at constant magnetic rotor flux. It follows the first part paper, in which the attention has been directed towards the control of constant stator flux and constant magnetization flux. The working algorithm is the same as the one described in Part 1, the analysis being done under the following two aspects: the mechanical characteristics and the speed control at constant torque or constant power, respectively. In the second part of this paper, a comparative analysis of the main performance indicators associated to the three control methods (constant stator flux, constant magnetizing flux and constant rotor flux) is presented. Among the quantities envisaged, there are the efficiency, power factor, input current and the rms value of the needed supply voltage.

articleTitle: An analysis of specific parameters regarding the extraction of crude oil with an electric driven pumping unit
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper refers to the electric drive of the crude oil beam pumping unit, with a squirrel-cage asynchronous motor controlled in the Direct Torque Control technique. A complete pumping cycle has two strokes: one upward in which the electric machine works in motor mode and one downward in which the machine works in generator mode, which can be considered a braking regime. By determining the variation of the mechanical parameters of the pumping unit (total load torque, operating speed, oil flow and pumping phase), obtained with primary level programs, a Simulink diagram of the electric drive has been developed in order to obtain other important parameters of the electric drive, which can operate at different frequencies. An important conclusion of this paper is that the energy dissipated by the electric drive during the downward stroke period has significant values in all the studied situations and it is necessary to carry out studies regarding its recovery possibilities.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Models for Nonlinear Loads with Firing Angle control Devices Part II - Modeling
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: A frequency domain model for a one thyristor rectifier is developed for the first time in the literature. This model consists in polynomials in terms of the RMS value V1 and the initial phase phase (V1) corresponding to the voltage fundamental component. A polynomial of this kind gives the RMS value I2k-1 or the initial phase φ2k-1 of the (2k-1)-th current harmonic for a certain value of the firing angle α. This model is built based on measurements of I2k-1 and φ2k-1 on V1 and phase (V1) for a certain range of firing angles. Two interpolation techniques are used to obtain the above dependences for a new firing angle value. This result is validated by the comparison of the interpolated current waveform with the measured one.

articleTitle: Novel Spoke-Type Ferrite-Magnet Generators for Micro-Wind Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper aims at providing a comprehensive review based on design analysis of relevant new spoke-type ferrite-magnet generator topologies for appropriate use in micro-wind power applications. An analytical overview of innovative designs - originated from radial-flux and axial-flux permanent-magnet machines - able to fulfill the challenging requirements for direct-driven low-speed micro-wind generators is presented.

Author Keywords: radial-flux and axial-flux spoke-type ferrite-magnet generators

articleTitle: Intelligent Management of the Hot Rolling Mill Influence of the Automation System on Hot Rolling Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The complex Rolling Mill Process requires a rigorous and Intelligent Management. In this paper the authors envisaged the management of the Hot Rolling Mill in Galati County. At the finishing mill exit the hot strip receives the final values of thickness, width, flatness, mechanical properties and appearance topology. The automation system of the finishing train, manages the Rolling Mill process through a hierarchical structure. Through the execution elements, i.e. the hydraulic motors and stations, the desired final physical sizes of the strip will be provided. The reference values of the rolling mill process are provided from the mathematical model and a rolling scheme. The hierarchical control system is composed of two levels of automation, that communicate with each other, each level making calculations and adjustments in the appropriate loop according to well-defined algorithms. The feedback of each control loop is ensured from the adequate sensors and the transducers and they are compared with the reference values in order to obtain the physical realization of the hot mill process. All sizes are carefully monitored and recorded continuously in a database, both the initial and final ones. The hierarchical architecture of the rolling line is provided in the Second Section. The Settings of the specific parameters on the Hot Rolling Mill Process from Galati County is shown in the third Section. The operation of the cooling system is performed through the specific case study, as shown in the fourth Section. The conclusion is provided in the last Section.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Filtering in FPGA
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In this paper we used two different filtering methods for ECG signal processing. The signal is processed in Spartan-3E FPGA circuits using a mean filter with a 16-sample window first, and then using a low-pass filter generated by the FDA Tool utility in the MATLAB environment. Both filtering algorithms are implemented in FPGAs using the Verilog Hardware Description Language. The results are compared with each other, then with those obtained in the MATLAB environment. The paper also analyses the hardware resources in the FPGA required for the two implementations. The signal was previously recorded using a 12-bit acquisition system and a sampling rate of 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Logistic regression classification model identifying drugs of abuse based on their ATR-FTIR spectra: Case study on LASSO and Ridge regularization methods
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: We are presenting a comparative study of two variable selection methods, i.e. Ridge and LASSO regularization methods that were used for selecting the most adequate coefficients for error minimization. The logistic regression model was used for the detection (classification) of new analogues of high risk drugs of abuse belonging to the 2C-x and DOx classes of hallucinogenic amphetamines, based on their ATR-FTIR spectra. The results indicate that the LASSO method yields the best results. Although both methods generate remarkably sensitive class identity recognition tools, the system based on the Ridge regularization method is less selective than that using the LASSO method.

articleTitle: The results of the electromagnetic field measurements performed on a military maritime ship to determine the effectiveness of a radio-absorbent material
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The authors present part of experimental results to the field measurements carried out on a military ship aimed to find-out the efficiency of a new shielding material. In this respect, the authors propose the use of a new method to determine the efficiency of a screen, especially when the measurements are not performed in a specialized laboratory.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Networks designed to identify NBOMe hallucinogens based on the most sensitive molecular descriptors
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Drugs are largely responsible for a high percentage of the public health problems and drug-related mortality worldwide. The illicit drug market is constantly evolving in order to circumvent controls and confiscations. NBOMe is a newly discovered class of hallucinogenic drugs. Their representative synthetic derivative is 25I-NBOMe, which is sold on illicit channels in the form of powder or blotter paper. This study presents and compares a series of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) designed to screen for NBOMe hallucinogens. The database is composed of 160 illicit drugs, such as NBOMe hallucinogens, narcotics, sympathomimetic amines and other potent analgesics, as well as some of their major precursors. The molecular structures of the main NBOMe hallucinogens were first optimized using the Hyperchem 8.03 software. Then, topological, 3D- MoRSE and constitutional descriptors, as well as functional groups of these compounds have been determined by using the Dragon 5.5 software. Then ANNs have been built by using only the most selective descriptors. Their accuracy was compared based on several figures of merit. The impact of variable selection on ANN performance and is also analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: The energetic performances of control at constant magnetic flux of an induction traction motor: Part 1 - Performances of control at constant stator flux and constant magnetizing flux
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper presents an algorithm for the analysis of energetic performances of an induction motor controlled at constant stator flux and constant magnetizing flux, destined to the electric traction of autonomous vehicles. Due to the operation at voltage and frequency different from the rated values, this is a complex issue that requires a procedure for estimating variable parameters. In this goal, an algorithm for estimating the resistance and inductance of the magnetizing circuit was developed first, based on which the energetic analysis of the control at constant stator flux and constant magnetizing flux was performed. The analysis is performed considering the mechanical characteristics, as well as the speed control at constant torque or constant power, respectively. The estimation of core losses and electromotive voltage is also required for the calculation of energetic indicators.

articleTitle: Compensating Capacitor Voltage Fuzzy Hysteresis Control for a Direct Current Controlled Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The regulation of the dc-link voltage for the shunt active power filters is typically done by a proportional integrative controller. The use of a fuzzy controller for this job eliminates the laborious tuning process, which is replaced by the membership functions definition. To validate the results, a comparative study was done between the fuzzy controller and the reference proportional-integrative controller performance. The fuzzy voltage controller has an aperiodic response, with good voltage regulation, but because of the high output ripple, a first order, low pass filter is necessary. The low pass filter reduces the ripple to a level at which the distortion produced to the compensated current becomes insignificant, without noticeable affecting the controller performance. On the other hand, the filter presence changes the fuzzy controller response from aperiodic to oscillatory, but the created oscillation is low, lower than the PI controller corresponding oscillation. A comparative study was also done between the unfiltered fuzzy controller and the filtered fuzzy controller performance. For the case of the fuzzy controller a compromise must be made between high output ripple and poor regulation. Although, for the direct current control, the active charging current is low, so the output ripple can be reduced without visibly affecting the voltage regulation.

articleTitle: The influence of the connecting elements of the three-phase shunt active filters - in the Common Network Connection Point - on the efficiency of the filtering process
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In the paper, the influence of the values of the elements of the network connecting block of a three-phase active filter of shunt type on the THD of the current delivered by the source supplying a non-linear load is analyzed. For the usual connecting elements (coil, coil and resistor, etc.) are visualized the variation ranges of their parameters which ensures the lowest THD current and, implicitly, the lowest harmonic content in the current transmitted on the line between the source and the strong nonlinear load. These studies aim to validate a methodology for choosing / sizing these connecting elements - in CNCP - for a wide range - as driven power - of shunt type three-phase active filters.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Biomass Plant Energy Efficieny
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Nowadays the diversification of energy production, especially with renewable sources, is one of the objectives of sustainable development and the characterization of their functioning and parameters is the subject of interest of the researchers. For green power plants running on biomass, the amount needed is variable depending on several factors. This article aims to determine a dependence between the input-output parameters of cogeneration plant, namely between the energy contained in the biomass, depending on the calorific power and mass of raw material, and electrical power generated. Using the data collected in the last 3 years from a cogeneration plant running on biomass in Romania since 2014, an interpolation method and an original ordering of annual values are used to obtain the accurate dependence input-output.

articleTitle: Fuzzy speed control in drive systems with voltage inverters and induction motors
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the implementation and validation of a fuzzy logic speed controller, for a voltage inverter and asynchronous motor drive system. The fuzzy controller has an aperiodic response, and gives good speed regulation at high mechanical load changes. On the other hand, it gives a small stationary error, and the controller is instable at very low speed or high speed change. The speed controller input variables are the speed error and the speed error change, and the output variable is the frequency of the inverter output voltage. The inverter gating signals were obtained using the classical sinusoidal PWM modulation. The sinusoidal control voltages of the PWM modulator were obtained as a function of frequency (speed controller output). Changing the direction of rotation was obtained by imposing negative speed. As a result, the fuzzy controller outputs negative frequency which is evaluated by the PWM modulator changing the phase shift. The control system has only one control loop which is the speed control loop, so the current through the motor windings is not limited. Although, the current stress is low, even at time moments when the output frequency has a steep change or when the motor load is connected. The controller implementation and validation was accomplished on a comprehensive drive system built in the Matlab Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Model free control of a 2DOF robotic arm using video feedback
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In this paper we present our approach on solving the positioning problem for the Tool Center Point (TCP) of a 2 Degrees of Freedom (DOF) robotic arm similar to the way a human solves positioning tasks. The presented method relies on visual feedback and angular positions of the elements and eliminates from the equation the need to know the elements lengths, contrary to classical robotics where positioning is done through the direct and inverse kinematics method. The paper presents hardware, software and the general architecture of the system and also the proposed positioning algorithm. The scope of this research is to expand the area where robotics can be used, toward unstructured environments, where with help of vision systems, robots can successfully complete tasks.

articleTitle: The Efficiency of an Underwater Inductive Charging System for AUVs Based on Truncated Coils
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper proposes an underwater inductive charging system of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) with the scope of extending their autonomy. The novelty of the proposed solution consists in the geometry of the power system - based on truncated coils, adapted to the hydrodynamic geometry of the AUV. The analysis of the inductively coupled resonant circuits is performed by analytical method, whereas the study of the magnetic field generated by the transmission coil is performed by means of numerical software tools. The study is completed by experimentally determining the power transfer efficiency of the truncated coils system.

articleTitle: Route Planning Strategy for Smart Tourism Services Development
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper proposes a route planning strategy integrated in a software platform, capable to offer personalized visiting program for touristic zones. The presented solution is based on the utilization of multimodal intelligent transportation systems, having the potential to contribute to the development of smart low-carbon cities. The considered approach is based on two different routing algorithms: an exact one, the Martins algorithm, applied for the initial scheduling of the travel and NSGA-II, and a faster metaheuristic algorithm to tackle momentary modifications generated by new decisions and unexpected events. The multi-objective scheduling strategy was implemented and tested for medium, time dependent transport networks. In order to develop smart tourism services, the platform also integrates the conceptual and implementation support offered by cloud computing.

articleTitle: Sample Value Ordering for Audio Reversible Data Hiding
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Pixel value ordering (PVO) was shown to be an efficient technique for high-fidelity reversible data hiding in images. This paper proposes an audio reversible data hiding scheme inspired by PVO, namely sample value ordering (SVO). Large uniform areas are uncommon in natural images, but sections of silence are relatively common in audio samples. In order to properly exploit the nature of the host audio file, a block-based approach is employed. Non-overlapping blocks are classified into three categories: smooth, somewhat complex and complex. All samples from a smooth block are considered as possible hosts using a classic histogram shifting based approach. For somewhat complex blocks, only the maximum and minimum sample values are used for data hiding with the PVO inspired SVO. Complex blocks remain unchanged.

articleTitle: Interference Challenges on board Military Ships
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In an interference network, several receivers of information communicate with each other on the same channel. Simultaneous transmission of information will result in severe cochannel interference at an information receiver. Two major effects can occur: obtaining a low signal-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) and a high risk of information leakage. Thus, on board military ships, a major importance is the class of signals that fall within the receiver band called the interference channel. There are many measures proposed to reduce the effects of interference of disturbances: frequency management, emission time management, location management, direction management. These methods are inefficient if the useful signal propagation to the receiver antenna is done in multiple ways. Therefore, it becomes important to study co-channel interference in order to identify the anti-disturbance solutions from the design and design phase of the communication systems. The multitude of disturbing signals aboard the military ship can affect the restoration of the locally generated carrier with direct effects on the demodulated signal. The authors studied the co-channel interference between the Double Sideband Suppressed Carrier Amplitude Modulation communications (DSB-SC) designing a Matlab-Simulink simulation program. DSB-SC systems were chosen because, among the analogue communication systems, they proved to be the most resistant disruption systems. In the case of inter-channel communication systems using DSB-SC, they are particularly resistant as long as the demodulation of the locally generated carrier is in phase with the useful signal carrier. The authors provide an attractive study based on inter-channel communication systems using DSB-SC. The analysis results obtained by DSB-SC implementation on the Matlab / Simulink platform are highlighted in this paper.

articleTitle: Finite State Predictive Torque Control with Switching Table for Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In the last ten years, Finite State Predictive Torque Control (FS-PTC) is being studied extensively due to many great features such as simple structure, easy implementation, low torque ripple. However, FS-PTC has two main disadvantages. Firstly, the computational burden is large because it uses all possible vectors within a predictive horizon. Specially, the computational burden rises very fast, if converter has many voltage vectors or predictive horizon is long. Secondly, the choice of weighting factors are difficult. This paper proposes FS-PTC with switching table structure to eliminate the choice of weighting factor and reduce computational burden.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Radiated Compromising Emanations for Computer Monitors
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: To highlight the necessity of applying additional protective measures to the equipment that processes critical information, comparative measurements were performed for two display devices, one commercial and the other shielded, in order to detect the compromised emanations that they generate. The amplitude of the electromagnetic signals generated by the two displays were compared and their compromising emanations were captured and processed in order to recover the displayed images. The monitors were tested in a TEMPEST laboratory consisting of a semi-anechoic test chamber and a control shielded chamber.

articleTitle: Modeling of Pre-University Education Units Electric Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Due to the large number of pre-university education units, about 27% of the total public institutions in our country, it was necessary to analyze the consumption and the quality of the electric energy and to measure in situ the parameters of that energy. Using the values provided by a data acquisition system, this paper developed a polynomial regression in the Matlab-Simulink programming environment to model the characteristics of electricity consumers in a high school. An analysis is made of the methods for optimizing the consumption of electric energy and its quality indicators are evaluated, taking into account the national and international standards as well as the internal norms. Considering that the energy profile of this consumer is common to other public institutions, because of the energy consuming equipment, finally, the solution for the supply of renewable energy sources is proposed.

articleTitle: Microgrid Power Infrastructure for Critical Operations
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The current utility grid is a bulk power system, inflexible, centralised controlled. The insertion of the renewable energy sources (RES) into the utility grid is a real challenge for most electric operators. Recently, the cyber-attacks on power grid raise the problem of continuity in ensuring the electrical energy to the critical infrastructures. In order to assure the electrical energy to the critical consumers, the authors of this paper propose a viable solution based on the microgrids. Moreover, the proposed microgrid control allows the insertion of the additional power from the RES, the normal operation in both cases: grid-connected and standalone. Through the appropriate frequency and voltage control, the power quality of the microgrid is obtained in conditions of normal operations and perturbation. The proposed solution agrees well in case of blackouts or grid-attack. The autonomy of the microgrid makes the solution to be a good candidate for the military camp.

articleTitle: Cyber-Physical Systems for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Following the advent of cyber-attacks, but also the expansion of the worldwide digitalization, cyber security has become a national priority in many states of the world. Both the knowledge development, through the new industrial revolution (Industry 4.0) and recent cyber-attacks, lead to the adoption of rapid cyber security measures. The cyber-physical systems are based on the safety, reliability, and availability. The cyber-physical systems are the foundation of the critical infrastructures. The critical infrastructures are related to the nation prosperity, industry, and to the state security assurance. From cause and effect point of view, a chronological development of the cyber security legislative framework is presented. The main protection tools in cyber security of the critical infrastructures are emphasized by highlighting their main features.

articleTitle: Updating an electric propulsion UAV device for long range missions
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper presents the actual method used in upgrading an electric propulsion UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) (commonly known as drones) device with 2.45 m wingspan and weighing 8 kg. The device, endowed with a ROXXY Brushless Outrunner D63-72 230kV engine and a 14-inch propeller, has been successfully tested in various test flights. The paper explicitly presents the electric and electronic layouts, as well as the solutions identified for increasing its range by including a telemetry system based on the national GSM network.

articleTitle: Active Power Filter Control Strategy Choosing by M-Tool Application
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Power quality is an important aspect studied nowadays. Related to energy efficiency in electricity the power quality is a very important concept which give us a view regarding the energy efficiency. The main responsible for a poor power quality is the non-linear loads, who's number is increasing every day. The active power filters (APF) is a solution to improve the power quality. The construction of this APF is requiring knowledge about the power quality and about the known control strategies. Those control strategies must be able to deal with the poor power quality. This paper presents an electronic solution: M-tool which is an application able to indicate the most appropriated control strategy in certain conditions. This application was developed in the project:, Knowledge Transfer Regarding the Energy Efficiency Increase and Intelligent Power Systems” (acronym CRESC-INTEL).

articleTitle: Management of a photovoltaic-battery-based microgrid in a prosumer context
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Prosumers are households that are both producers and consumers of electricity. In this paper, an Energy Management System (EMS) for a DC-microgrid-based prosumer is designed and simulated, whose aim is to coordinate operation of a photovoltaic (PV) system and a battery for supplying a DC load; interaction with the utility grid - modelled as an infinite-power source - is minimized, such that power is either injected or drawn only when strictly necessary. The PV system and the battery are paralleled on a common DC-link by means of a boost converter and a synchronous buck converter, respectively, while an inverter ensures connection to the utility grid. In order to design and simulate the individual components of the microgrid, MATLAB®/Simulink® tools were used. During the study, different operating scenarios were created with respect to the PV power, load and the state of charge (SoC) of the battery. Thus, the following operation modes were identified: following mode, discharge mode, charging mode - referring to the battery operating modes that depend of its SoC. The aim of the EMS is to ensure the requirements of a prosumer application and switch between these different modes. Simulation results have shown that the developed EMS can achieve effective coordination within the microgrid, and all goals are reached.

articleTitle: Segmentation and machine learning techniques applied to automatic detection of diseases from eye-fundus retina images
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Here are presented some methods of retina image processing for retina image segmentation of blood vessels, using the ARIA and B-COSFIRE filters methods, with noise reduction. Eye-fundus images are used for experiments for noise removal with KSVD and BM3D methods also we use an image contrast enhancement (CLAHE) method: Contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization. Is presented also an efficient method of image segmentation based on a nature inspired optimization technique namely Particle Swarm Optimization.. In the end machine learning techniques are applied to automatic detection of diseases from retina eye-fundus images with automatic classification.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper focuses on several recent applications of deep learning approaches to a broad range of tasks, including a personal view on current trends, critical issues, and limitations of the technology.

articleTitle: A General Approach for Change Detection in Vibration Signals with Application in Machine Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper presents a general approach for change detection in vibration signals with application in machine health monitoring using advanced signal processing techniques. These techniques mainly include change detection (CD) algorithms, independent component analysis, time-frequency analysis, energy concentration evaluation, as auxiliary tools for feature extraction and analysis of vibration signals. They operate in a reduced dimension space, highlight and enhance the changes in signals. Finally, the paper presents a case study in health status monitoring of an industrial pump.

articleTitle: Indoor Drone Application with Acoustic Localization
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the design of a rotary wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and the method used for this UAV to determine its mathematical location indoors. The optimal method used for the location determination was established upon research. By reducing the signal loss caused by the indoor area and with the use of acoustic localization that measure distance by 3-dimensional vectors with velocity of ultrasonic sound wave, the determined method allowed the instantaneous observation of the UAV's mathematical location in 3-dimensional space. Furthermore, this method enabled a balanced and efficient autonomous flight indoors.

articleTitle: Electrical Equipment Safety Analysis and Simulation: Case Study: Transformer's Malfunctions
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The role of safety and resiliency of the power system is a concept already applied in several sectors, although making its way harder in the power system sector. This paper considers the progress made by implementing the new technologies in terms of security systems and draws attention to the vulnerabilities arising with this kind of integration. The main benefit consists of active shielding against presumed attacks, yet once succeeding an attack can determine serious consequences. As a risk scenario, it is considered a cyber-attack that aims to change the security parameters of an electrical transformer station. Here, included is a model regarding the effects of such an attack. As a safety measure, to counteract such a possible attack, one can propose the use of encryption methods for the transformer's parameters.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Decision Making Support Systems for Activated Sludge Process
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Activated sludge process is an important step in the wastewater treatment. It is a difficult to control process because of its complex nonlinear behavior. The studied water treatment plant has its own particularities due to the nature of its customers (mainly surrounding refineries). The proposed decision making and monitoring support systems are based on the available operating data from a Romanian wastewater treatment plant. Although activated sludge analytical models for this highly nonlinear process are available in the literature, data mining techniques provide also reliable results. The paper emphasizes the parameters correlations (under the form of proposed rules) that can be used for inferential measuring, thus decreasing the costs of on line analysis. Other found rules can be used as support system for the wastewater treatment plant operator.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Model for an Electrical Cargo Ship
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The electric propulsion of cargo ships is not used on a large scale, being preferred only for special vessels. The paper develops a simple and precise dynamic model for a cargo ship, which allows study of the behavior of the electric motor - propulsion system - ship in the two variants Fixed Pitch Propeller (FPP) and Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP). The results obtained by simulation indicate the variant FPP as being more favorable from all points of view: maximum propulsion efficiency, reduced propulsion system costs, good use of the electric engine and increased maneuverability of the ship.

articleTitle: A Solution for Reducing Harmonic Regime and Reactive Power Absorbed by a Cycloconverter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the analysis of the operation of a high-power cycloconverter with a load type R + L: the harmonics and reactive regime with respect to the load and the supply network. Based on this analysis a solution is proposed to reduce harmonics and to compensate the reactive power absorbed from the network using an active power filter with indirect control. The solution is validated by numerical simulation in the SimPower Systems environment and is characterized by a simple implementation and outstanding static and dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Aspects of Features Selection and Extraction from Time-Frequency Images of Vibration Signals
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The research domain of the paper is the time-frequency image processing. Firstly, a comparison among the features selection and extraction methods from time-frequency images of vibration signals in bearings with faults is made. Both time and frequency methods are considered and discussed, from classification performance point of view. A new method of feature selection based on the decomposition of time-frequency images in sub-bands is introduced. For each sub-band, discrete cosine transform is applied. The coefficients of the transform are features which must be processed for classification task. Distance based classifier is considered with vectors of features of various lengths. Computer based experiments are conducted with real data from a benchmark database with vibration signals generated by various type and size of faults. The results are very encouraging and show the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Intelligent Protection of a Power Supply System for Electric Consumers without Access to the Low Voltage Line
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The research activity refers to the synthesis of the electronic equipment of global protection related to an efficient system for capturing the electric energy from the high voltage grid for the purpose of supplying high quality energy to electric consumers. The main objective of the paper is to present the protection from the input of the power supply system. After analyzing the main needs and types of protection encountered today in the composition of power supply systems we proceed to the synthesis of the block diagram for the implementation of the global protection. An advanced solution is to implement global protection with a intelligent numerical relay. Analysis of global protection is checked by simulation in the LabVIEW virtual environment. The modeling and simulation of the global protection function is performed for the following types: over and under voltage protection; over and under frequency protection; protection against overcurrent. Virtual tools designed, built and presented in this paper can also be successfully used in educational activity during specialized classes at colleges and universities.

articleTitle: Disaster management system
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The project has as a priority to contribute to the intervention and implementation of an emergency plan in case of an earthquake, by developing a system of solutions that will ensure the continuity of the activity as follows: - Monitoring: evaluating the performance of the building or dangerous infrastructures in real time; - Alarm: offers alerts when the design parameters are exceeded and transforms the information into useful data; - Emergency interventions: implement rapid response procedures leading to decision-making measures; - Communication and Dissemination: manages the transmission of information that is imperative for making business continuity decisions. During an emergency situation, the faster the community resumes daily activity, the less the losses are reduced. The alarm system transforms a building system into a network of infrastructures monitored in the case of seismic events. The two-way collective information offers a complete picture of the earthquake effect, followed by the road to the previous activity or restoration. The conclusion will be to avoid unnecessary evacuations, stopping work processes and minimizing response times, stress and reducing panic. The proposed solution to ensure continuity of activity in the event of an earthquake, must be available on the desktop and smartphone.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Electric Traction UAVs
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In today's context, drones are getting ever more popular. The advantages of operating such devices are evident due to the need for cutting down on polluting gas emissions, to which the use of electric traction UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) are a viable solution. From this point of view, the present paper proposes an optimization algorithm for designing electric traction UAVs. Making use of a database containing the specifications of a number of 24 brushless engines, and taking into account the operating requirements such as the useful load, flight time, etc., the proposed algorithm, together with the software application, is the optimal construction solution for the project design.

articleTitle: Optimization of Convolutional Neural Networks for Face Recognition Problems Aimed to Resources Constrained Platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In this paper is proposed a method to obtain high recognition rates of face recognition problems using low complexity convolutional neural networks, tailored for resource-constrained computing platforms. Different variants of CNN architectures were considered and thoroughly evaluated on datasets such as YouTube Faces Database and Aligned Face Dataset for Face Recognition. We experiment by training our architectures on various computing platforms including CPU, GPU and evaluate performances such as recognition rates, prediction estimation, throughput and latency. In optimizing the specific parameters, a trade-off between a good accuracy and a low complexity was considered.

articleTitle: On Noise Estimation of MIMO Wireless Channels for Low-computational IoT devices
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: In Internet of Things (IoT), devices and sensors connect each other and exchange information over the Internet. Many IoT devices have limitations in storage capabilities, processing and energy resources. Hence, the wireless networks must be able to dynamically change the transmission rate, according with the channel state fluctuations, with small adequate bit error rate (BER) of communications. The channel noise characteristics are important for management system. Their estimation is realized with varying degrees of uncertainly, considering the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Since IoT devices have limited processing capabilities, low-computational methods for channel noise estimation are necessary. In this paper, aspects of channel noise estimation are studied, using smaller subsets of the received symbols. Different SNRs and parameter values of subsets are taken into account and simulation results are presented. Good estimation of noise characteristics with lower computational complexity can be obtained.

articleTitle: The Capacitor Voltage Balancing Problem in FS-PTC for Induction Motor fed by 3L-NPC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The requirement of capacitor voltage balancing occupies an important position in controlling Three-Level Neutral Point Clamped (3L-NPC) inverter. It becomes even more important when 3L-NPC inverter is applied to drives system. In the past ten-year, Finite State Predictive Torque Control (FS-PTC) for Induction Motor (IM) is gaining huge attention from researchers in the field of electric drive system. The use of 3L-NPC inverter for FS-PTC is extremely complex because in addition to controlling torque and stator flux, FS-PTC also maintain capacitor voltage balancing. This problem can be solved by using the cost function with three optimal components: optimal component of torque error, optimal component of stator flux error and optimal component capacitor voltage error. However, choosing 2 weighting factors for this cost function is difficult because there is not basis to choose. This paper build a new method to remove the optimal component of capacitor voltage error from the cost function. It is done by selecting the appropriate vectors for the capacitor voltage balancing before calculating the predicted values of torque and stator flux and after finding the optimal voltage vector. This selection is made through output of a hysteresis controller.

articleTitle: Consumption Optimization Aspects in Renewal Energy Systems Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: One of the main characteristics of renewal energy is that it is available at a specific moment in time, thus we can consider this a renewal energy generation time pattern. Similar, in turn demand for energy, or consumption have a specific time pattern. In the ideal case to minimize energy storage challenges and to efficiently use energy, generation time pattern should match as much as possible with consumption energy pattern. In the current article we improve this pattern match between generation and consumption using artificial neural network.

articleTitle: Indoor Visible Light Communications demonstration: University Campus Radio Station transmitted through the lighting system
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Due to numerous advantages, Visible Light Communications are considered to have high potential in various areas. Thus, both new indoor and outdoor applications are being constantly identified. In this paper, we present a demonstration in which the VLC technology is used to transmit the University of Suceava campus radio station through the lighting system. This pilot project is currently implemented in the Optical Communications laboratory, with possible development within other laboratories or in the campus area. Thus, using a rather simple optical receiver based on a phototransistor, one can listen to the campus radio station received through the optical carrier. The purpose of this project is to demonstrate a simple application of VLC and to popularize this technology as an alternative and/or complement to the RF solution.

articleTitle: Reactive power compensation for a PV park connected at a long distance
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Reducing the production of electrical energy from classical sources in favor of renewable sources of electricity has become a global priority. In most cases, renewable energy sources are located at a considerable distance from the point of consumption, due to this fact the transport and distribution grids are big enough to consume reactive power due to their own inductance L, but also to generate reactive power due to the capacity C. To solve the problem of uncontrolled injection of capacitive reactive power, in this paper is propose the use of an active power filter mounted on the low voltage side. The active power filter is controlled by the synchronous algorithm (dq) method, and summed the phase angle between voltage and current on the medium voltage side with the angle of synchronization with the grid voltage on the low voltage side. Thus reducing the capacitive reactive power generated by the cable.

articleTitle: Personal seismograph system - a functional prototype
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Disaster management system consists of administrative policies, decisions and operational activities that are linked to various stages of disasters at all levels. With the passing of the years and the evolution of the society, it can be noticed that the extreme phenomena are becoming more and more numerous. About 90% of all disaster victims belong to poor countries or areas where the seismic risk is very high. The current interest is to monitor and evaluate these natural phenomena more closely in order to reduce losses. This work is intended to show the functioning of a seismograph system implementation being done on a Raspberry model 3B + development board together with a mpu6050 accelerometer-gyroscope module. The information recorded by the mpu 6050 module will be analyzed and stored in a database. of graph. Every vibration felt by the accelerometer-gyroscope module will send an SMS alert to the mobile phone through an IFTTT service. The notification will contain the type of produced earthquake according to the magnitude (minor, light, moderate, strong) as well as its classification in a number of degrees on the Richter scale and the time of its production. In this way, a database can be created for a more accurate assessment of the intensity distribution of the recorded earthquake.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Extreme Learning Machine using Various Computing Platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on testing the performance of an optimized extreme learning machine (ELM) algorithm using various resources-constrained computational platforms, to be used in autonomous intelligent vehicles. The purpose of this comparative study is to find the best suited embedded computational platform for future use in an experimental autonomous mobile robot, where computing power, responsiveness and power consumption are key to further development. The aforementioned algorithm was used as a benchmarking tool in this performance review, but also as an important starting point for processing large amounts of different data types from the robots' sensorial units. For now, the conducted experiments are limited to pre-trained datasets, to have a precise output of the very same data type.

articleTitle: Change Detection in EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to provide a method for change detection in subject's status, based on analysis of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals, recorded during a calibration stage. The results are sought to be applied in medical diagnosis and in online brain-computer interfaces. The status of the subject may refer to: emotions, sensorial activity and intentions of muscular activity. The specific target is to design a systematic detection method of the change in EEG running signals. The particular case presented in the paper concerns a relaxed subject, who opens or closes the eyes, but the method can be extended to other state changes. The proposed method includes: separation of the frequency bands of the EEG signals, computing the Root Mean Square (RMS) value inside that band, over a moving window, and thresholding. The selection of the feature, the choice of the threshold value and the choice of the window length are explained in detail. Experimental results concerning the proposed method, applied to real data EEG signals, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Reactive power compensation for consumers connected at long-distances
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The main objective of the distribution and transport grids is to transport the electricity to the end users with efficiency, quality and reliability, which requires to minimizing the energy losses. Because the electricity is produced outside the consumption points, it involves the existence of long-distance transport and distribute lines. To solve the problem regarding the reactive power flow, an active power filter (APF) mounted on the low voltage side is suggested to be used in this paper. This solution is exemplified for consumers connected to medium voltage grid and where the connection point is situated at long distances.

articleTitle: System for Acquisition of Energy Parameters for Consumers Without Access to the Low Voltage Line
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The production of electrical energy in the isolated areas (farms, chalets, vacation houses, etc.), that don't have distribution networks, is in continuous growth. Taking this into consideration, it is built an integrated system for supply from electrical airlines IT (SIA-LEA 110...400kV) for building low voltage sources, for supplying isolated consumers and also building of a monitoring system for the energetic activity for these. The paper presents the hardware and software architecture of the acquisition and control system from the local consumer level, system that assures the necessary information for the description of the behavior of the isolated consumers in real exploitation conditions, for growing the safety in functioning and of the availability of the electrical energy supply equipments. In this way, it is presented: The block diagram of the acquisition and control system; The type and role of the component equipments of the acquisition and control system: electrical network parameters analyzer (EEM-MA600 Phoenix Contac); programmable logic controller (Inline - ILC Phoenix Contact).

articleTitle: Microgrid Optimal Power Flow for Increased Security
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The AC microgrids ensure both uninterrupted power supply to the consumer and secure operation. The components of the proposed microgrid are divided into energy sources and critical consumers. The energy sources consist of an energy storage system, a renewable energy source and a Diesel-generator as a back-up power system. The problems of modern microgrids are related to the cost of the supplied energy, but also to the efficiency. In this paper, the authors propose a strategy for the optimal use of clean energy sources for both constant and variable loads. In this way, the microgrid allows the use of more sustainable energy sources for the environment. The microgrid architecture allows the use of local energy sources and can deliver the electrical energy in both operation modes: island and grid-connected, under quality conditions of the energy. In this way, the microgrids offer higher security in the energy supply of the consumers, compared to the national energy system. The paper presents the problem of optimized control of power flow under energy constraints, as well as the obtained numerical results.

articleTitle: Understanding pedestrian behaviour with pose estimation and recurrent networks
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Early detection of pedestrians, quick understanding of their behavior and prediction of their intention are of extreme importance in the quest to the 5th level of autonomous driving. The development of deep learning techniques for pose estimation, both in terms of quality and speed, advertise pose estimation as a highly informative representation for human figures present in an image. With the help of pose keypoints we aim to classify short sequences of images in different types of pedestrian behaviors such as standing or walking, crossing, speeding up, waving. For this we propose a set of features based on pose estimations and two recurrent architectures, one with single output, and one with multiple output. We train and evaluate our models on different subsets of JAAD dataset in order to deal with the imbalanced classes.

articleTitle: BCONV - ELM: Binary Weights Convolutional Neural Network Simulator based on Keras/Tensorflow, for Low Complexity Implementations
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: A deep investigation of the possibility to minimize complexity, while keeping accuracy at its highest values is considered, centered around the idea of building specialized convolutional neural network architectures, tailored for resource-constrained platforms. Starting from the idea used in extreme learning machines where a nonlinear expander with random weights is combined with a rapidly trained linear adaptive unit as the output layer, a simulator working under Keras/Tensorflow is developed. As a consequence of using Keras backend operators, GPU or CPU support is available using the same code. The resulting simulator (made freely available) is composed of three main modules: i) A convolutional expander, using kernels with randomly generated binary weights; ii) An extreme learning machine for rapidly tuning the random kernels for the best performance; iii) A Keras based multi-layer perceptron (usually operated as Adaline or 0 hidden layer with weights quantization) as a compact output layer of BCONV-ELM. Performance evaluation on several benchmark datasets show that with a proper tuning of the convolutional layers structure, good accuracies are achieved without additional dense hidden layers thus minimizing the required computational resources.

articleTitle: On Human Faces Thermal Image Processing for Classification Purposes
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: This paper presents some results from a preliminary work on human faces thermal image processing for classification purposes. The main task is to find right representations and descriptors/features for high recognition rates. A data base with thermal images is created using people in various states, which reveals happiness, normal and sadness states. A toolbox based on Matlab modeling and simulation environment was designed and developed. The toolbox has specialized functions for image conversion from color to gray levels, format image conversion, image segmentation, objects detection and localization, face contours, image compression and analysis. Various data transform for image processing are considered, accompanied by information-based transforms, e.g. Renyi transforms. Classification is considered and it is based on similarity of the patterns. The results are very encouraging and show the flexibility of the toolbox and the potential of the proposed methods based on Discrete Cosines Transform (DCT) for feature selection and extraction.

articleTitle: Background Noise in Radiation Sensors and Cameras with Collimators and Noise Economic Impact
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: The background radiation noise contributes to the total noise and signal quality degradation from radiation sensors and cameras. We present equations for the equivalent noise and signal to noise ratio for uncollimated and collimated sensors and cameras. This background noise issue is especially important for applications in medicine where it dictates the image quality at specified radiation intensity and, as a consequence, cancer risks.

articleTitle: A Study on the Implementation of HVDC for Power System Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Modern power systems have an ever-increasing power demand; an increase in power supply must answer this increase in demand. One method to increase the reliable supply of power requires the interconnection of multiple power systems. The main problems associated with the interconnection of multiple electrical networks include the need for the synchronization between networks, losses associated with long transmission lines, increase in the short circuit current, and a possible reduction in network stability. The implementation of high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems is a possible solution to such limitations, resulting in a higher capacity, more reliable, and a more efficient power system. A preamble exploring the power flow in the AC transmission systems continues with the description of the operation of the HVDC transmission link. Consequently, the paper proposes an analysis regarding the effects induced by the presence of the HVDC in the interconnected power systems. In the case of the study presented in the paper further on, subjecting an HVDC transmission link, there is a load flow analysis followed by a transient one; both simulations performed utilizing the ETAP software package. Results-driven conclusions about the effects of the HVDC transmission lines on power systems complete the paper.

articleTitle: Toward a mixed visible light communications and ranging system for automotive applications
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Optical Wireless Communications are emerging as promising alternative to radiofrequency and microwave communications in order to respond to the increasing demand for data transfer and to the expanding area of wireless applications. In this context, this paper provides a short overview of OWC technologies and focuses on their usage in automotive applications. Thus, vehicular Visible Light Communications and Visible Light Ranging systems recently developed by our research groups are presented in order to set the path toward designing a mixed visible light communications and ranging system for automotive applications based on standard car lighting system.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation and Optimization of Dual-Heating System
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Heating systems are of importance both from the point of view of social life and as energy consumers and producers of pollutants. The global energy crisis, environmental pollution and divergent global energy policies have imposed new solutions for heating systems. Dual heating systems are one of the viable and future solutions. In this sense, this article proposes a dual heating system consisting of a gas and an electric one whose operation is dictated by a complex monitoring and control system. An algorithm and a cost optimization function are proposed, with which the control strategy of the two systems is chosen. The comparative results obtained from the measurements and the simulation of the proposed algorithm justify the introduction of the dual heating system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conchoidal Radiation Collimators and Shields
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEEE)
abstract: Noise in radiation camera and camera resolution are largely determined by the radiation attenuation characteristics of the collimators. We analyze the attenuation of cylindrical and conchoidal collimators. We also analyze the possibility of combining conchoidal radiation collimator with adjustable and reconfigurable radiation shields and the potential advantages that can be obtained. We show that the combination can improve the collimation, when the direction of radiation is known, and can also act as a directional filter. The contributions of the study are the analysis of the attenuation of cylindrical and conchoidal collimators in a radiation bandwidth and a configuration for the correction of the directivity pattern in conchoidal collimators for radiation cameras.
